s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent vertical misalignment with elevation deficit
salient_findings: Elevation deficit of the right eye
Anomalous band in the right orbit
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle
key_facts: 52-year-old woman
History of long-standing diplopia
Persistent vertical misalignment
Orthotropic in primary position
Elevation deficit of the right eye
Previous surgical excision of anomalous band in right orbit
No improvement in motility after surgery
Diplopia remained stable in primary gaze
MRI of orbits showed unremarkable globes
No measured proptosis
Retroocular fat, optic nerves and sheaths, optic chiasm, and brain parenchyma appeared normal
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion noted medial to the medial rectus muscle

shortlist.label: Brown syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of persistent vertical misalignment and elevation deficit

shortlist.label: Superior oblique tendon syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the patient's history of diplopia and elevation deficit

shortlist.label: Adhesive syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the patient's persistent vertical misalignment and previous surgical excision of anomalous band

shortlist.label: Monocular elevation deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the patient's clinical presentation of elevation deficit in the right eye

shortlist.label: Double elevator palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the patient's history of diplopia and elevation deficit, and the presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion

raw.rationale: The presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle, which is unchanged from the previous study and has signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle, suggests a fibrotic or adhesive process. This, combined with the history of previous surgical excision of an anomalous band and persistent diplopia, supports the diagnosis of Adhesive syndrome.

rejected.label: Brown syndrome
rejected.why: Typically characterized by limited elevation in adduction, which is not the primary complaint in this case

rejected.label: Superior oblique tendon syndrome
rejected.why: Usually presents with torsional diplopia and limited rotation, not the primary findings in this patient

rejected.label: Monocular elevation deficiency
rejected.why: Involves a deficiency in elevation of one eye, but does not typically involve a soft-tissue lesion as seen on MRI

rejected.label: Double elevator palsy
rejected.why: Characterized by impaired elevation of both eyes, which is not consistent with the orthotropic position in primary gaze and elevation deficit limited to one eye in this case
